text: Sessions authenticate with the owner's claude.ai subscription via Claude Code login, not an Anthropic API key
author: claude-code
alternatives: Console API key with spend limit

text: The tester session commits tests that pass only on correct behavior, before a fresh implementer session runs
author: claude-code

text: Live per-session steering uses Claude Code Remote Control from the Claude app, not a custom app
author: claude-code
rationale: Remote Control only attaches to interactive sessions; --max-turns and --max-budget-usd are print-mode only

text: Escalation follows a four-tier rubric: interrupt now, interrupt if idle with a default and deadline, digest, log only; one notification per cause
author: claude-code

text: Where should tier 1 and tier 2 escalations reach the owner: Claude app, Linear, or a push service such as ntfy?
author: claude-code

text: How many issues may run in parallel on one subscription?
author: claude-code

text: How should work be split into disjoint tasks before dispatch? Deferred by the owner.
author: claude-code

text: Escalations are recorded in Linear (escalation and needs-decision labels, one shared issue per cross-cutting cause, a daily digest issue) and pinged through a separate phone push channel
author: claude-code
rationale: Poller writes to Linear with the owner's own API key, so Linear likely does not notify the owner of those actions
revisit: Push service choice pending research; Linear self-notification behaviour unverified
cost_if_wrong: If Linear does notify on own-key actions, the push channel is redundant
choice: Linear as record, separate push as ping

text: Integrations beyond the core loop (calendar free/busy, claude.ai connectors, others) are added later, held by the poller and notifier; agents get only what their task needs
author: claude-code
choice: defer integrations; least access for agents

text: A session started by a script under tmux with claude --remote-control <name> '<prompt>' runs the prompt and connects to Remote Control, after a one-time folder-trust prompt per directory
author: claude-code

text: Local sessions find and message each other with ListAgents/SendMessage, but ListAgents shows auto-generated names (e.g. spike-repo-c2), not the --remote-control name, and lists every Claude session on the machine
author: claude-code

text: claude -p with --strict-mcp-config and an empty --mcp-config sees no MCP servers, including claude.ai connectors; without it, claude.ai connectors load
author: claude-code

evidence.ref: spike 2026-10-09, CLI 2.1.293; interactive mode not tested

text: Sessions started from inside a Claude Code session inherit its CLAUDE_CODE_* environment (messaging socket, session id, task list id); the poller must start agents with a clean environment, keeping CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
author: claude-code

text: Subscription usage is machine-readable only through the status line JSON (rate_limits.five_hour / seven_day used_percentage and resets_at); /usage has no JSON form and -p output has no window fields
author: claude-code

text: What share of the 5-hour and weekly limits may agents use, leaving headroom for the owner's own sessions?
author: claude-code

text: The poller stops starting new issues above configurable usage thresholds, defaulting to 60% of the 5-hour window and 50% of the weekly limit; per-task fit estimation is deferred
author: claude-code
rationale: Owner rates limits as low priority now; an agent's self-estimate of usage is unreliable without per-issue history
revisit: Once per-issue usage history exists, estimate fit from it
choice: fixed admission thresholds from status line rate_limits
alternatives: agents estimate whether their task fits the remaining limits

text: Agents only ever run as Claude Code sessions on the owner's subscription; no direct Anthropic API or Agent SDK use, and the launcher strips ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
author: claude-code
revisit: If Codex support is wanted; only the launcher knows which CLI runs

text: Components: one script (poller, launcher, supervisor, publisher, notifier) on a systemd timer under flock, interactive Claude Code agent sessions per issue, a SQLite claims ledger, and a pre-commit hook per worktree; agents never push, open PRs or change Linear status
author: claude-code
choice: single orchestrator script plus agent sessions

text: Implementation is Python with uv, following the nimblefox-template tooling: mise-pinned tools, ruff, pyrefly, pytest, a justfile with fmt/lint/test/check, and a ./setup script
author: claude-code
rationale: Owner's preferred language and existing dev setup
alternatives: TypeScript on Bun with the official Linear SDK

text: Everything runs on one dedicated VM that is the sandbox; agent sessions run directly on it in tmux, without per-session Docker containers
author: claude-code
revisit: If sessions need isolation from each other beyond worktrees

text: Agents get a read-only fine-grained GitHub token for gh; only the publisher holds a write token
author: claude-code

text: Use built-in Claude Code features where they exist (Remote Control, SendMessage/ListAgents, usage auto-continue, status line, --mcp-config, app push); build only the service, the launcher and a Claude Code plugin holding the tester/implementer skills, escalation rubric and handoff hooks
author: claude-code

text: Issue flow: pick, admit (usage, cap, path claims, dependencies), prepare worktree, tester session, implementer session with handoff restarts past 60% context, script publishes; failures retry once from the handoff note, then escalate needs-decision
author: claude-code

text: Configuration has three layers: defaults in ~/.config/linear-agents/config.toml, a per-issue agent block in the description, and live steering through Remote Control
author: claude-code

text: Testing: pytest unit tests with GraphQL fixtures, process tests against a fake claude binary, a throwaway-repo test for the pre-commit hook, claude plugin eval cases for the escalation rubric, and a manual end-to-end smoke test
author: claude-code

text: The design spec at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-09-linear-agents-design.md is approved for planning
author: claude-code

text: A session started in a new git worktree under an already-trusted folder gets no folder-trust prompt, so worktrees under one trusted root start unattended
author: claude-code

text: Agent sessions, worktrees and agent-written checks run as a separate unprivileged agent Unix user; the orchestrator runs as the owner and alone holds the Linear key and GitHub write token
author: claude-code
rationale: A same-user agent in auto permission mode can read mode-600 secrets and run the publisher itself, so the spec's Access table would be unenforced
cost_if_wrong: Adds vm-setup steps, a sudoers rule, a second claude login, and cross-user git handoff in the publisher
choice: separate agent user, reached through sudo -u agent from the owner, tmux server in the agent user's lingering systemd user service
alternatives: same user, boundary as policy only

text: A Type=oneshot unit kills every process left in its cgroup when ExecStart exits, so a tmux server forked by the tick dies at the end of each tick
author: claude-code

text: Agents share the orchestrator's Unix user for now; the agent access boundary in the spec is policy, enforced only by the VM being the sandbox, HTTPS-only remotes with no stored credentials, and a missing agent token failing the launch
author: claude-code
rationale: Owner judged the separate user not worth its setup cost at this stage
revisit: Before agents work on repos or accounts whose compromise matters beyond this VM
alternatives: separate unprivileged agent user via sudo -u

text: Agents share the orchestrator's Unix user on a machine the owner trusts; the spec's agent access rules are behavioural (prompt, skills, hook, read-only token in env), not an enforced boundary
author: claude-code
revisit: Before running on a machine or with repos where an agent reading the Linear key or write token matters
alternatives: separate unprivileged agent user via sudo -u

text: A rerun on a kept branch that still contains the first run's tester commit starts at the implementer with the remembered base and tester commits.
author: claude-code
rationale: A fresh tester on a branch that already has the tests adds nothing and blocks, and the tests_touched guard loses the first run's tests
choice: Remember base_sha and tester_sha per issue in ledger meta when the tester finishes; on start, resume at impl if the branch contains tester_sha

text: Ticks that fail for reasons other than Linear are counted in ledger meta and page once (tier 1, global) at the same threshold as Linear failures, while the tick still exits non-zero.
author: claude-code
rationale: A failing tmux service otherwise fails every tick with no page
choice: tick_failures counter reset on a clean tick, cause tick-failing

text: release always kills the session and deletes the claim, warning instead of failing when the Linear issue or the worktree cannot be handled.
author: claude-code
rationale: A deleted issue or half-done release otherwise leaves a claim nothing can clear
choice: Warn and continue on LinearError, git and OS errors
alternatives: Abort release on any failed step
